10. OHSS:

-3.1 – 8%.
-Moderate/severe = 1.1%.
-Hospital admission = 0.3%

Risk Factors:

•PCOD
•Previous OHSS
• AMH
• Antral count
⇨Exposure of HCG or LH after ovarian stimulation by FSH.

 

 

Release of VEGF.

 

 

Vascular permeability

 

 

Osmolality

Serum sodium these 3 indicate OHSS

HCT

Types:

-Early: within 7 days of HCG trigger.
-Late: 10 or more days after HCG.

Symptoms:

-Abdominal bloating.
-Abd discomfort, Pain.
-Nausea vomiting
-UOP
-Leg swelling.
-Vulval swelling.
-Associated morbidities.

Thrombosis:

- 0.7 – 10% in severe OHSS

-Commonly Arterial – Neurological signs/symptoms.

- Several weeks after settled OHSS Disease.

- loss of vision.

- neck pain.

 

Women suspected of OHSS.

1.History:
•Onset of symptoms in relation to trigger.
•Type of trigger
•No of eggs retrieved.
•No of final follicles.
•No of embryos transferred.
•PCOD – diagnosed.
2.Examination:

General:

- Dehydration, Edema, HR, R/R, B.P, Weigh.

Abdominal:

1.ASCITIES 2. Palpable mass3.Peritonism4. Abdominal girth

Respiratory :

effusion, pneumonia pulmonary edema

3.Investigations:
•FBC
•HCT
•CRP
•Urea, Electrolytes Na, K.
•Osmolality
•LFTS - albumin.

- enzymes.

•Coagulation: fibrinogen, Antithrombin.
•HCG
•USG
-Ovarian size
-Ascites
•Doppler
-If torsion suspected.
4.Other Tests
-D – Dimers
-ABGS
-ECG
-ECHO
-CXR
-CTPA, V/Q scan.

 

Classification of OHSS & Management

Mild:

•Mild bloating
•Mild pain
•Ovarian size <8cm3.

Moderate:

•Mod pain
•NV
•USG Ascites
•Size 8 – 12.

OUTPATIENT MANAGEMENT

Mild + Mod + selected severe cases:

- fluid intake – drink to thirst @ least 1liter/D.

- UOP monitoring

- Detailed counselling of worsening signs:

⇨ Abd girth
⇨Pain
⇨Weight gain shortness of breath
⇨HR, T B.P.
⇨UOP (<1000ml/24hrs, +ve fluid balance).
⇨HCT
⇨Contact details should be provided

- Avoid NSAIDS,

Paracetamol, Opioids are given to relive pain.

- follow up: 2 – 3 days

Worsening signs = urgent review

- Lab investigations: repeated if worsening signs.

- paracentesis: OPD Basis (TAS, TVS).

- GnRH Ant, Dopamine agonist insufficient evidence but beneficial role.

- VTE prophylaxis in moderate OHSS=> stocking or LMWH if risk factor for VTE present.

Hospital Admission Criteria:

1.Critical OHSS + Severe OHSS (selected)
2.Unable to come for follow up
3.Unable to achieve pain control
4.Unable to take oral fluids due to NV
5.Worsening signs.

Severe OHSS:

-Clinical Ascites + Hydrothorax.
-Oliguria (<300ml/D or <30ml/hour).
-HCT > 0.45
-Na <135
-Osmolality <282
-K >5
-Albumin <35g/l
-Ovarian Size > 12cm3.

OPD/inpatient management:

MDT

Monitoring once/day in admitted Pts.

-Weight
-Abd Girth
-I/O
-CBC, S/E, LFTS, osmolality, HCT
⇨LMW prophylaxis till admission or 1st .

Critical OHSS

-Tense Ascites + Hydrothorax
-HCT > 0.55

-TLC > 25,000.
-Oliguria/anuria
-ARDS
-Thromboembolism

 

Inpatient Management:

-MDT
-ICU care

Monitoring ONCE – Daily in Admitted pts.

-Weight
-Abdominal Girth
-I/O record
-CBC, HCT, LFTS, S/E, osmolality.

More Frequent monitoring:

-Critical OHSS.
-Thromboembolism or other complications.

VTE prophylaxis given.

MDT:

-Critical OHSS
-Severe OHSS with persistent dehydration and hemoconcentration.
-Case reporting in severe and critical OHSS.

Fluid Management:

-Oral route guided by thirst
-I/V fluid if unable to take orally
⇨Crystalloids – initially
⇨Colloids-more effective
⇨ Human albumin solution 25%

50 – 100g over 4 hours

Repeated every 4 – 12 hours

⇨Strict I/O record
-Persistent hemoconcentration despite I/V fluids => MDT – Anesthetist for invasive monitoring.
-Persistent oliguria => Paracentesis.
-Oliguria:

Fluids

 

Persistent oliguria => Paracentesis.

Avoid diuretics => in MDT setting diuretics have role.

Indications for paracentasis:

-Severe abdominal distension and pain due to ascites.
-SOB due to abdominal distention and ascites.
-Oliguria despite adequate volume replacement.
•USG Guided.
•I/V colloid in case of paracentesis.
•Early paracentesis in moderate and severe OHSS prevent disease progression

Surgical Treatment:

-Torsion, rupture, Ectopic

 

Laparoscopic untwisting

•Pregnancy after OHSS

Risk of PTB & Pre-Eclampsia.
